hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $2$.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than $2$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 2. A line running to the right starts at 2 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $2>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 2. A line running to the left starts at 2 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/8cb2d0321f4ae95a88cf86fbae91e6932225b57b)

The graph of $x =2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at 2.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e3da225abb83ea339da6a3e1efe464303c6a6675)

The first number shown on the number line is $-5$, but $-5$ is not part of the inequality graph.  The graph of $-5<x$ looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the right starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/d2a35478327aef385727781d1c6d3c8c501e8446)
